text:
tessa: FYI ran an integration test that simulates 300 concurrent onboarding flows and hit fd exhaustion. Root cause seems tied to streaming Generator usage in background goroutines + auth rotation.

omar: Can you paste the handler snippet?

tessa: Minimal problematic pattern we used in the sample app: 
```go
func onboard(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  go func() {
    ctx := r.Context()
    s, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
    if err != nil { return }
    for s.Next() { /* forward tokens */ }
    // no Close(), detached goroutine
  }()
  w.WriteHeader(202)
}
```

vik: Two separate things colliding: (1) detached goroutine never closes the stream, and (2) token refresh happens synchronously inside the SDK send loop so transient retries prolong the network op, holding the fd. Combined they leak resources under concurrency.

omar: Short-term fixes we discussed: update the sample app quickstart to always create a child ctx with timeout/cancel, call defer s.Close(), and ensure draining the stream until Next() == false. Add a small FAQ note about auth refresh extending send latency.

tessa: I pushed a sample-app patch that replaces the detach pattern with a supervised worker pattern and shows select { case <-ctx.Done(): s.Close() } handling. PR: devex/sample#920

docs-bot: New PR suggested: docs#1287 "Go: generator streaming cleanup and auth rotation guidance"

vik: Medium-term: SDK ergonomics improvements we want to explore: Add Stream.Done() <-chan struct{} and an explicit Close(ctx) API, plus a lightweight GC finalizer that logs at debug level if a Stream was garbage-collected without Close. Also add an open_streams metric + transient retry cap for streaming send loops.

omar: We should avoid breaking changes. Proposal: add additive methods (Done(), CloseWithContext(ctx)) and document the recommended pattern. Then in v2 promote io.Closer-like semantics. Also prototype a go vet analyzer to flag `go func(){ ... r.Context() ... Stream(...) }()` patterns in our sample repos.

tessa: I'll file an RFC for the SDK changes and include some microbenchmarks showing the leak reproduction. Ops: can you add a short alert when open_streams exceeds threshold in staging?

ops-bot: Alert rule created: infra/alerts#stream-leak-threshold (triggers when open_generator_streams > 200 for 5m).

omar: Great. For the immediate docs update please include the minimal code example plus a one-paragraph "Why this happens" explaining auth rotation interaction. That seems to fix the bulk of onboarding confusion. :thumbsup:
